title: Design how a machine is earned rather than bought
ask: Daniel ruled Q-88 option b — the mark-2 robot is earned by demonstration, by having actually used a mark-1 — and asked for the mark-1 to be triggered too, suggesting: after a player spends more than half a day's energy watering. That turns the placeholder shop rule off for machines and makes owning one mean something.
first_action: Write the design note for both triggers: what the sim already counts that could prove them, what the player sees when one fires, and what happens to the shop entries the machines have today.
source_message: Daniel ruled Q-88 option b — the mark-2 robot is earned by demonstration, by having actually used a mark-1 — and asked for the mark-1 to be triggered too, suggesting: after a player spends more than half a day's energy watering. That turns the placeholder shop rule off for machines and makes owning one mean something.
result: Already completed on main by f2e821a (2026-09-23), docs/design/06-bots-and-training.md, “Earning the first two robots.” The note turns Daniel’s Q-88 option b and his mark-1 watering suggestion into two proofs: 11 successful player water Actions in one day (330 of 600 normal energy units, reset at sleep), then a placed mark-1’s first successful taught water or till Action. It names excluded events, the locked-to-bright shop cards and seed-box cue, the existing 150g/400g [Playtest] purchases after proof, and the saved/replayed latch plus old-save ownership migration. docs/DECISION_LOG.md and docs/DESIGNER_QUEUE.md record the same ruling. Separate implementation card w9f46b7286df reports the subsequent build in 35714f2; this card requested the design note, so no duplicate design or implementation patch was made.
